root_cause.text: The CXL port subsystem lacks reference counting to guarantee the parent port device remains alive during the lifetime of a child port, causing use-after-free when `cxl_detach_ep()` accesses `parent_port` after it has been freed during bottom-up removal.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message explicitly states "both of these issues stem from the absence of a lifetime guarantee between a child port and its parent port." The patch adds `get_device(dev->parent)` in `cxl_port_alloc()` and `put_device(dev->parent)` in `cxl_port_release()` to hold a reference to the parent, preventing its premature deallocation.

candidates.rationale: Assigns parent device pointer without incrementing reference count, allowing parent port to be freed while still referenced by child.
Accesses parent_port->depth without ensuring parent remains alive; contributes to use-after-free when parent is freed early.
Stores a pointer to parent_dport (associated with parent port) without taking a reference, indirectly tying child lifetime to parent.
Conditional that selects the freeing path; the lack of check for active children before freeing makes this a vulnerable site.
Frees a CXL root port without verifying that all child ports have been detached, enabling use-after-free when child later accesses parent.
Branches to non-root freeing path; participates in the same lack of reference-counting discipline.
Frees a non-root port without ensuring that no child ports still reference this port as parent, directly causing the use-after-free.

Accesses parent_port->depth without ensuring the parent remains alive, contributing to use-after-free when the parent is freed early.
Stores a pointer to parent_dport associated with the parent port without taking a reference, indirectly tying child lifetime to the parent.
Conditional that selects the freeing path; the lack of a check for active children before freeing makes this a vulnerable site.
Frees a CXL root port without verifying that all child ports have been detached, enabling use-after-free when a child later accesses the freed parent.
Frees a non-root port without ensuring that no child ports still reference this port as parent, directly causing use-after-free.
Branches to the non-root freeing path; participates in the same lack of reference-counting discipline and is part of the vulnerable code flow.
